name: Town Center around the Basilica
description: The compact core clusters around the white Basilica of Our Lady of Copacabana and Avenida 6 de Agosto, the main strip lined with hostels, tour agencies, cafes, and market stalls. It is the most walkable, liveliest part of town, though every block feels steep at altitude.

name: Lakefront and Harbour
description: The shoreline along the harbour is where launches depart for Isla del Sol and Isla de la Luna, and where trout stalls and lakefront eateries line the water. It offers the best sunset views and the freshest air, with a relaxed, open feel beside Lake Titicaca.
bestFor: Sunset lovers and island day trips
pros: Fresh trout right by the water

name: Cerro Calvario Hillside
description: The hill above town carries the stations of the cross to a summit crowned with shrines and panoramic views over the lake and rooftops. The slopes below hold quieter guesthouses. It is a steep, breathless climb at this altitude, but the sunset payoff is unforgettable.

name: Isla del Sol
description: A short boat ride offshore, Isla del Sol is the Inca creation-myth birthplace of the sun, with terraced ridgeline trails, ruins, and basic village lodgings. Staying overnight trades wifi and comfort for silence, star-filled skies, and the purest Lake Titicaca experience away from town.
